title: Baseball Card Grading Service (2026)
verdict: A baseball card grading service has to cope with a century of card stock, and AGS handles it by measuring each card and adjusting tolerances for vintage.

Send the card you will auction to PSA if the premium covers its fee. Send the rest of your baseball cards somewhere fast and flat-priced. That is the split most sellers land on, and AGS fits the second job.

sections.h: What you get for the fee
list: A grade from 1 to 10 with decimal precision.
Eight subgrades: centering, corners, edges and surface, front and back.
A 3D heightmap of the surface, color-coded from green to red.
High-resolution images and centering data for both sides.
A sealed PMMA slab with the cert number on the label.

ranking.fit: Sellers who want baseball cards back in weeks with eight subgrades to show a buyer.
ranking.lacks: Standard-size cards only. Ask before sending thick patch cards.
ranking.note: AGS lists basketball, football, baseball, soccer and racing cards, modern and vintage, including signed cards.

ranking.fit: Pre-war and vintage sets, where SGC has long standing.
ranking.lacks: Reported at $50 a card since September 2026. No longer cheap.

ranking.fit: Anyone sending a key rookie to auction, where the PSA label widens the bidder pool.
ranking.lacks: Value-based fees and 25 to 45 business days or more on listed tiers.

ranking.fit: Sports collectors who want a major grader at $10 to $13 a card.
ranking.lacks: Fees step up at $500, $1,000 and $3,000 of card value.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want a Beckett label with subgrades and no fee tied to card value.

ranking.fit: Small sellers who would rather not choose a tier.
ranking.lacks: A small buyer pool. ISA slabs sell for less on most cards.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

Every slab comes with the evidence. The digital report shows eight subgrades, centering data, high-resolution images and a color-coded heightmap of the surface, red on major flaws and green on clean areas. You can download it or share it by link, and the scan stays on file against the cert number.

The price does not move with the card. AGS charges $18 per card whatever it is worth, with bulk tiers from $15 at 30 cards. PSA and SGC price by declared value and CGC caps each tier by card value, so a card that turns out to be worth more can cost more to grade.

faq.q: What is a good baseball card grading service?
faq.a: AGS for a measured grade on baseball cards at a flat $18. PSA for the strongest resale on key rookies. SGC for vintage.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.

Signed cards are accepted for grading. If you need the autograph itself authenticated, use a grader that sells that service. Beckett lists a $5 autograph add-on, and CGC offers autograph authentication.
Yes: basketball, football, baseball, soccer and racing cards, modern and vintage, including chrome finishes. Sports cards are $18 at the standard rate, or $18, $23 and $33 on the bulk tiers.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.
